claims.text: As-cast equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is a homogeneous simple solid solution.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in its simple solid-solution state has moderate hardness and strength with favorable plasticity.
The moderate hardness and strength of simple-solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi result from a lack of nanoscale precipitates that would strongly pin dislocations.
A controlled sub-critical heat treatment can nucleate nanoscale precipitates in CoCrFeNiTi without causing a full phase transformation.
Nanoscale precipitates in CoCrFeNiTi act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
The as-cast alloy has minimal lattice distortion.
Minimal lattice distortion and the absence of precipitate obstacles facilitate easy dislocation slip in as-cast CoCrFeNiTi.
Easy dislocation slip produces moderate hardness and high plasticity in as-cast CoCrFeNiTi.
Heat-treatment-induced fine precipitates will pin dislocations in CoCrFeNiTi.
Precipitate-induced dislocation pinning will increase the yield strength and hardness of CoCrFeNiTi.
Precipitate-induced dislocation pinning will reduce the plasticity of CoCrFeNiTi.
Heat-treated CoCrFeNiTi will have higher hardness and yield strength than the as-cast alloy.
Heat-treated CoCrFeNiTi will have lower plastic strain than the as-cast alloy.
Heat treatment will change dislocation behavior from predominantly planar slip to a more pinned or disrupted pattern.
The proposed mechanism applies under compressive loading from approximately 25 °C to 600 °C, provided extensive phase transformation does not occur.
